# costperrun

> A free calculator for what one multi-step AI agent run actually costs. It models the quadratic growth in billed input tokens caused by an agent re-sending its entire context on every step, across 31 models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI, Moonshot and DeepSeek.

Language models are stateless. An agent must re-send its whole history on every step, so total input tokens across N steps come out as:

    N × (system + user) + (output + tool_result) × N × (N−1) / 2

The second term is quadratic. Doubling the step count roughly quadruples the input cost. Most LLM pricing calculators price a single request, which is correct for a chatbot and understates agent cost by several times.

Worked example, a 12-step agent with a 2,000-token system prompt, a 500-token task, and 400 output plus 1,200 tool-result tokens per step:

- Raw conversation length: 21,700 tokens
- Billed input at a 0% retry rate: 135,600 tokens, a 6.2x multiplier
- Billed input at a 10% retry rate: 149,160 tokens, a 6.9x multiplier

The multiplier grows with step count: about 1.7x at 3 steps, 6.2x at 12, 10.3x at 20, 25.3x at 50 and 50.3x at 100.

The three levers that reduce it, in order of effect: prompt caching, because cache reads cost roughly 90% less and most of the bill is context re-sent verbatim; step count, because it is superlinear while price is linear; and tool-result size, because every tool result is re-sent by every later step.

## Pages

- [Calculator](https://costperrun.com/): The tool itself. Set steps, tool-result size, retry rate and cache hit rate, then compare 31 models, see cost attribution by component, and read the per-step accumulation table. Runs entirely in the browser.
- [Method and FAQ](https://costperrun.com/#method): Derivation of the formula, the worked example, the three levers ranked, and a plain statement of what the model does not cover.

- [Subscription vs API](https://costperrun.com/subscription-vs-api/): Turns a Claude Pro or Max plan price into the number of agent runs the plan has to beat at API rates, using the same context-accumulation model, with a break-even by model. Plan usage limits are not published as token or message counts, so the page does not model the quota. Only Anthropic's plan prices are listed.

## Data

- [models.json](https://costperrun.com/models.json): The canonical pricing dataset. Every rate carries the provider's own pricing URL and the date it was verified.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/pop3zxcv/costperrun): Full source. Stale prices can be reported as issues.

## Limitations

- Retries are modelled as a flat multiplier on total cost. Real retries occur at a specific context depth, so failures late in a run are under-counted.
- Cache hit rate is a single figure rather than per-prefix.
- Batch API and cache writes are options, off by default. Batch applies each provider's published discount (50% at OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, 20% at xAI; none at DeepSeek, Meta or Moonshot K3). Cache writes bill 1.25x the input rate for Anthropic and OpenAI at their shortest retention. Long-context pricing tiers are not modelled.
- Providers use different tokenizers, so cross-vendor token counts are approximate. This holds inside Anthropic's lineup too: Claude 4.7 and later, which is every Claude model here except Haiku 4.5, use a newer tokenizer producing about 30% more tokens for the same text than Haiku 4.5. A single token count compared across those models understates what Sonnet 5.5 bills for the same work.
- Tiered pricing is flattened, and the direction of the error differs by provider. DeepSeek bills peak and off-peak, with off-peak half of peak; the figures here are peak, so a run scheduled off-peak costs about half what is shown. OpenAI, xAI, Google and Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 raise rates on large requests, and the figures here are the base tier, so a long agent is undercharged. Haiku 5.5 changes gear first, at 100K prompt tokens, where input, output and cache rates all rise 5x. Grok and Gemini change gear at 200K tokens, Grok by doubling every rate. OpenAI's threshold is 272K, where the whole request is rebilled at 2x input and 1.5x output, taking GPT-6 Astra from $10/$50 to $20/$75. On the default workload the largest single request is about 81K tokens at 50 steps, so this only bites at roughly 62 steps on Haiku 5.5, 125 on Grok and Gemini and 170 on OpenAI. A 100-step Haiku 5.5 run costs about 3.5 times the figure shown.
- Output is a planning estimate, not a billing forecast.

## Notes

- Prices verified 28 October 2026 against each provider's own pricing page.
- Cache-hit rates are taken from each provider's published price. Most are 90% off input. The range runs from 75% off (Grok 4.6 and 4.7) to 98% off (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), and the default model, Claude Sonnet 5.5, is 95% off.
- GPT-5.6 Sol's $4/$20 is promotional, described by OpenAI as available at least through 21 November 2026. No successor rate is published.
- Claude Sonnet 5's $2/$10 was announced as introductory through 31 August 2026. Anthropic cancelled the scheduled increase to $3/$15 and $2/$10 is now the standard rate.
- Gemini 4 Argon is on an introductory rate of $2/$10 through 30 November 2026 and doubles to $4/$20 on 1 December 2026.
- Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.7 Flash and 3.8 Flash are on promotional rates of $0.75/$3.75 through 31 December 2026 and double on 1 January 2027.
- A Runs that complete the task slider (default 100%) shows cost per completed task: the cost of one run divided by the success rate, with failed runs still billed. Monthly spend and the per-model table stay per run.
- The model table reports the spread between the cheapest and priciest model that fits the workload.
- An optional panel compares the cost of one run with a person doing the same task, from minutes per task and a loaded hourly cost that the user enters. It reports the monthly saving and a break-even month against a one-time setup cost. It assumes every run completes the task and excludes review time and upkeep. No salary benchmark is built in.
- No tracking, no signup, no analytics. The Content-Security-Policy is `default-src 'none'`, so the page cannot make outbound requests.
